1.title: VT and SGN: Two Concepts, Two Styles
1.html:
VT (Vendanges Tardives, late harvest) and SGN (Sélection de Grains Nobles, selection of noble berries) are two special designations that can be added to Alsace or Alsace Grand Cru labels, representing Alsace's strictest top sweet wines — their sugar thresholds are extremely strict.

🍇 Vendanges Tardives (VT)
Late-picked grapes, usually harvested several weeks after the normal harvest, allowing them to reach overripeness (surmaturité). The wine keeps the variety's recognisable identity and aroma, adding the power of concentration and some noble-rot character.
🍄 Sélection de Grains Nobles (SGN)
Through several successive passes (tries successives), only berries infected with noble rot (Botrytis cinerea) are picked. Varietal identity becomes more subtle, replaced by flavours dominated by concentration and noble-rot character — intense aromas, a very powerful structure, a round, viscous palate and a long finish.

These two designations were officially recognised and named by a ministerial decree of 1 March 1984.
2.title: Only Four "Noble" Varieties
2.html:
VT and SGN can only come from the following four varieties:

Gewurztraminer
Pinot Gris
Riesling
Muscat
3.title: Strict Production Conditions
3.html:
• Must be hand-harvested
  • Must come from a single variety, declared and sold under that variety's name
  • The vintage must be shown
  • No chaptalisation or any other form of concentration treatment
  • A prior declaration to the local INAO office is required before harvest
  • Must pass both analytical and sensory (tasting) certification

Climate foundation: Alsace's semi-continental climate, with scarce autumn rainfall and abundant sunshine, is the ideal condition for grapes to undergo "passerillage" (drying and concentration) and for noble rot to develop, making late harvests and noble-rot selections far later than the normal harvest possible.
4.question: VT and SGN designations may come only from which four varieties?
4.options.3: Any variety, as long as the sugar level is met
4.explanation: The regulations expressly limit VT (Vendanges Tardives) and SGN (Sélection de Grains Nobles) to four "noble" varieties: Gewurztraminer, Pinot Gris, Riesling and Muscat. These four are also, in principle, the authorised varieties of Alsace Grand Cru (exceptions: Zotzenberg may use Sylvaner; Hengst, Kirchberg de Barr and Vorbourg may make Pinot Noir red wine from the 2022 vintage) — showing the consistent logic of Alsace reserving its highest rules for these four core noble varieties.
